headline_marked: [[OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra]] Cracks Enigma Message Unbroken Since 2005
headline: OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra Cracks Enigma Message Unbroken Since 2005
summary: AI model independently deciphers a complex German WWII Enigma message, revealing new insights into historical cryptography and AI capabilities.
details: On September 15, 2026, Carter Leffer confirmed that OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra had successfully broken the German Army Enigma message MVUEH from July 10, 1941. This specific message had resisted all decryption attempts since 2005, making its eventual break a significant cryptographic achievement.

The MVUEH message, logged as Nr. 172, was sent by tactical callsign 2ny and received by the SS-Totenkopf Quartiermeister (Ib) radio station. While another Enigma message from the same day, Nr. 173 (SIPVX), was broken in 2017, its recovered key differed slightly and did not help in deciphering MVUEH.

GPT-6 Astra's analysis revealed that the MVUEH key was substantially different from other keys of the same date, even using a different wheel order (253 instead of 512). The plaintext was also remarkably similar to message Nr. 173, differing only by twelve letters, partly due to an enciphering error in MVUEH.

Further analysis of the break uncovered errors in the transcription of the MVUEH ciphertext and indicated that the Enigma's left-hand wheel turnover at the 72nd letter complicated the decryption process. These factors may have contributed to the message remaining unbroken for so long.

Astonishingly, GPT-6 Astra performed the entire decryption process autonomously after being tasked by Leffer to analyze unbroken Enigma messages. The AI identified MVUEH as the most promising target and even hypothesized a connection to the plaintext of message Nr. 173.

The AI developed custom software for Enigma simulation and Bombe analysis, utilizing the repeated place name 'ROSENOW ROSENOW' as a crib. This focused approach ultimately led GPT-6 Astra to discover the correct key and plaintext for the MVUEH message within a short period.

Logs indicate GPT-6 Astra may have accessed information from a private collection, potentially referencing digitized archives from the German Bundesarchiv. This suggests the AI acted not just as a codebreaker but also as a sophisticated archival researcher, a behavior that would typically take a human researcher considerable time to replicate.

headline_marked: [[AI Has No Wisdom]] and Neither Will You, Says Tech Expert
headline: AI Has No Wisdom and Neither Will You, Says Tech Expert
summary: An expert argues that reliance on AI for coding will stunt developer growth, predicting a future where "NO-AI" policies become a competitive advantage.
details: The article argues that while AI can handle tedious tasks, over-reliance on it for coding will lead to unmaintainable codebases and hinder developer mastery. The core issue is that code maintainability and good architecture effects aren't immediately measurable, making them difficult for AI to optimize.

Current AI models struggle with tasks like code simplification, often creating non-reusable functions or failing to grasp the nuances of good design. This is because AI learns from existing code, much of which is already suboptimal, and lacks the immediate reward signals needed for complex architectural improvements.

The author expresses concern over a growing trend of developers using AI to write and read code, fearing this will prevent them from reaching true mastery. Without making choices, taking responsibility for mistakes, and learning from them, developers risk becoming passive users of AI rather than skilled practitioners.

While acknowledging AI as a powerful tool that can boost efficiency and handle 'boring' tasks, the piece emphasizes that it's just that: a tool. The author predicts that the current hype around AI will fade, and companies will eventually highlight 'NO-AI' policies as a sign of quality and expertise.

The piece suggests that the intuition of experienced software engineers, built through years of debugging and problem-solving, is something AI cannot replicate. This intuition allows experts to anticipate issues and make design choices that AI, focused on immediate metrics, cannot.

Ultimately, the author believes that the future of software development will involve a more discerning use of AI, where human expertise and judgment remain paramount. The prediction is that companies will eventually differentiate themselves by emphasizing human-led development over AI-generated code.
